settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic Bernoulli bandits with calibrated fairness (fairness regret)
unmapped: Objective is fairness regret: sum_t E[sum_i max(P*(i) - pi_t(i), 0)], deviation from calibrated policy selecting each arm with probability that its reward realization is highest
Exploration length C(eps_2, delta) depends on max_{i,j} D(r_i||r_j) (total variation between reward distributions)
settings.definition_quote: The fairness regret $\regret_f$ of a policy $\pi$ at time $t$ is: $\regret_f(t) \defn \E [ \sum_{ i = 1}^\narms \max( \Pr^*(i) - \pi_t(i), 0) | \boldsymbol{\theta} ]$. The cumulative fairness regret is defined as $\cregret_{f,T} \defn  \sum_{t = 1}^T \regret_f(t)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Dueling bandits under Plackett-Luce model with calibrated fairness
unmapped: Pairwise preferences follow a Plackett-Luce model p_ij = nu_i/(nu_i+nu_j)
Objective is fairness regret (deviation from calibrated policy)
settings.definition_quote: In a dueling bandit setting, at each time step $t$, the decision maker chooses two arms $a_t(1),a_t(2)$ to ``duel'' with each other. The decision maker doesn't observe the actual rewards ... but rather the outcome $\mathbbm{1}(r_{a_t(1)}(t) > r_{a_t(2)}(t)).$ ... we adopt the {\em Plackett-Luce} (PL) model

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: For any $\epsilon_2,\delta>0$, setting $C(\epsilon_2,\delta) := \frac{(2\max D(r_i||r_j)+1)^2}{2\epsilon^2_2}\log \frac{2}{\delta}$, we have that (\texttt{Fair\_SD\_TS}) is $(2,2\epsilon_2,\delta)$-fair w.r.t. total variation; and further it has fairness regret bounded as $R_{f,T} \leq \tilde{O}((kT)^{2/3})$.

results.notes: Quantity is fairness regret (deviation from calibrated policy), recorded as 'other'. Only a proof sketch; tuning of eps_2, delta depending on T taken from sketch. The (2,2eps_2,delta) smooth-fairness part is a property, not a regret bound, so not recorded separately.

tuning: C(eps_2,delta) = O((2 max D(r_i||r_j)+1)^2 k^2/(2 eps_2^2) log(2/delta))

source.quote: For any $\epsilon_2,\delta>0$, setting $C(\epsilon_2,\delta) \defn O(\frac{(2\max D(r_i||r_j)+1)^2k^2}{2\epsilon^2_2}\log \frac{2}{\delta})$, we have that (\texttt{Fair\_SD\_DTS}) is $(2,2\epsilon_2,\delta)$-fair w.r.t. total variation; and further it has fairness regret bounded as $R_{f,T} \leq \tilde{O}(\narms^{4/3}T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: Fairness regret recorded as 'other'. Proof deferred to full version; relies on Lemma rand:perturb.
